title.narrative: Strengthening Home Based Care through Orphan Support

description.narrative:
Integrated AIDS Project (IAP) is run by the Assumption Sisters Nairobi. IAP implements activities in Gatundu District curved from the larger Thika District in Central Province of Kenyan. The larger programme serves People living with HIV and AIDS (PLWHA) and their families including Orphans and Vulnerable Children (OVCs). The main project activities include VCT centres, HIV and AIDS and health education, OVC support activities and home based care (HBC).
The geographical coverage of the proposed project will be limited to three sub-locations namely; Kamwangi, Kanyoni and Mbici of Gathaite Location. Basic health services are lacking in the remote areas/sub-locations (commonly known to IAP as the Upper Zone) targeted. This project aspires to alleviate the suffering of PLWHA and OVCs by supporting communities in managing HIV and AIDS community facilities and investments for themselves.
A majority of OVCs live within dehumanizing conditions with very poor shelters, poor clothing, beddings, inadequate food, isolated and stigmatized by neighbours or close relatives and eventually dropping out of school due to lack of school fees and educational materials. The girl-child especially takes parental responsibilities when too young since she has practically to feed for her siblings. Such demands commonly militate the girl dropping from school, being sexually exploited, subsequent early pregnancy and at times early marriage. The boy-child easily falls prey of peers who recruit him in drug and substance abuse, is exploited as cheap labour while others resort to juvenile crime for survival.
Most guardians are elderly women and men left with the burden of starting to raise families of OVCs in old age. Majority of these guardians have no income of their own. The experience is overwhelming and traumatising following on loss and grief. The psychosocial trauma exhibited by both the guardians and the OVCs are of a complex nature leading to first level of depression.
Directly beneficiaries are OVCs as a result of AIDS. The proposed project will endeavour to provide the necessary care and support to the most vulnerable children in terms of economic empowerment, educational improvement, psychosocial support, community mobilisation and sensitisation for support of OVCs and awareness creation for the local leadership on the plight of OVCs. Secondary target beneficiaries are the guardians who are aged, sickly and lack resources to support OVCs under their care.
